top_choice_rationale: P001 credits a sharp, falsifiable prediction (Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states from time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling alone) and its first experimental test in HgTe quantum wells, with about two decades of transport and ARPES work confirming it; the discovery is mature and the narrow two-dimensional citation keeps three-dimensional work out. The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 2016 topology overlap are real weaknesses that should be recorded openly, but I do not find them disqualifying. P002 is second because its two-name allocation is cleaner and the magic-wavelength lattice is a genuine concept, though precision gains sit closer to the 2005 and 2012 lineage. P003 is third because the experimental credit rests on one name and the decisive experiments are still young. All three are preferable to no award.
